comments.text:
"Greek people will tell you, basically, all of this is indisputably Greek..."

Except no, Greek people will not tell you that. Not unless you ask some extreme irredentist who is stuck in the 19th century. I'm sorry, I like the funny, quick style of simplified recaps of history, but sometimes a little too much simplification becomes insulting. I am Greek and don't think that this view would represent any significant majority of people. Like, yes, obviously there are a lot of Greeks with roots from all over Turkey and especially these areas, people who have been violently expelled, too. But the claim that it's some kind of mainstream opinion that these places are "Greek" is not based in reality, and portrays us all like we are fervent nationalists. I've seen this before in videos explaining Greek culture, and they portray us like we are a nationalistic, hyperreligious, conservative monolith. It's, uh... it's reductive and a bit insulting.

As a sidenote, I'm not sure what the "Demotic" denotes on the map. Pontic and Demotic are two varieties of the Greek language, and while Pontic is from where it's shown, I am not aware of Demotic having an association with the coasts of Asia Minor. It might, but I at least haven't heard of it.
